summary: The study demonstrates the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to fabricate Al2O3 microtubes with precise wall thickness control on electrospun poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) microfiber templates. The ALD process uses TMA and DI H2O as precursors, and the wall thickness is controlled by the number of ALD cycles. The process is performed at 45 °C, and the resulting microtubes are characterized by FESEM and TEM. The study highlights the effectiveness of ALD in producing uniform, conformal Al2O3 microtubes with controlled thickness and smooth surfaces.
